discrepancy_resolution.mathematical_explanation: BIVARIATE TETRACHORIC ATTENUATION EFFECT: In the Monte Carlo thresholding model, latent continuous variables with correlation rho are discretized into ternary paired indicators D in {-1, 0, 1}. Discretization non-linearly attenuates the correlation (Pearson r_discrete < rho_latent) by a factor of ~0.65-0.75 for tail threshold cuts. Consequently, the manifest discrete ICC is ~0.13 (vs latent 0.20) and ~0.065 (vs latent 0.10), reducing realized DEFF from 2.05 to ~1.72. This lower standard error explains why simulated power (85.6%) is higher than asymptotic analytical power (80.7%).
discrepancy_resolution.auditor_recommendation: The analytical power of 80.7% should be retained as the CONSERVATIVE lower bound, while the simulated 85.6% reflects the manifest thresholding reality. Target N=2,850 safely satisfies both standards.
